links.outcome: Readability/accessibility of LLM clinician responses to simulated aphasic speech across models and configurations
links.effect: Accessibility varied by model and configuration; few-shot prompting and advanced reasoning generally yielded more accessible responses, and Gemini was superior under zero-shot standard reasoning.
links.quote: Few-shot prompting and advanced reasoning generally yielded more accessible clinician responses, whereas Gemini demonstrated superior accessibility under zero-shot, standard reasoning.

links.outcome: Readability of LLM clinician language measured with Flesch Reading Ease, Dale-Chall and composite score
links.effect: LLMs differ systematically in adapting clinician language to impaired speech; accessibility depended on model, prompting, and reasoning mode.
links.quote: LLMs differ systematically in their capacity to adapt clinician language to impaired speech.
